newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent paper steadies, cfds firmer.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent paper steadies, cfds firmer.

text.p: North Sea Brent outright levels and intermonth spreads were holding steady at the lower levels after putting the break on earlier falls, but shorter dated CFDs strengthened amid uncertainty over the value of spot Brent, traders said.

The Brent market backwardation contracted in early business with Feb/March easing around five cents from Thursday to trade at +25 and +26 cents, but the spread steadied in the afternoon largely ignoring the volatility of the futures market.
Feb/March Brent was pegged slightly wider at around +29/+34 cents with March futures creeping higher.

Traders read the slight widening as a sign that paper was beginning to echo a notionally firmer physical Brent market after a flurry of trade at big discounts this week cleared some of the end-Jan length, but traders were still uncertain about the real value of dated Brent.

Much of the business has been conducted between two U.S. trade houses, some of it at undisclosed levels, but traders were assessing the physical Brent market slightly better than the most recent confirmed traded levels of Feb Brent -24 cents.
Spot market uncertainty and volatile futures markets saw CFDs improving with next week's dates offered at March Brent +15 cents after early trade at +12 cents.
"The downside has been a little bit overdone recently but the front end uncertainty will keep the market pretty choppy with few players wanting to take lengthy positions," a trader said.
Five Brent dates from the February loading programme were due to turn wet on Friday and traders said the market would be eyeing what happens to these to get an idea of forward direction.
